chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It was so that whenever Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in a journey, or due to a reason of a need, would gather together Al-Zohr and Al Asr (Salāt), and between Al-Maghrib and Al-Isha (Salāt).

He (the narrator) said, 'And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with hastening the last Isha (Salāt) during the journey before the disappearing of the twilight (redness)'.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and rulings for combining prayers during travel in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi establishes the Sunnah of Jam' al-Qasr (combining and shortening prayers) during travel, reflecting the practical flexibility granted to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the Imams. It specifically clarifies the permissibility of hastening Isha before the disappearance of the red twilight (shafaq), a detail that Shia jurists utilize to distinguish between Jam' al-Taqdim (combining by earlyening) and Jam' al-Ta'khir (combining by delaying) in various travel scenarios.
